rapport_notes: Warm, friendly opener; good energy and attentiveness to customer throughout; natural conversational tone.
process_discipline_notes: No repeated differentiators; silence handling not explicitly tested (no open-ended questions with deliberate pause).

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "Do you have a few minutes to kind of go with me through your move on the 10th of September?" — asks for time but does not frame the ask with a promise of an accurate quote or anchor the value exchange.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: "before I kind of dive in to the what are the most important things I can answer for you on the call today if any?" — asked before probing begins.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says "I don't really have any major questions, so" — rep accepts this and moves to logistics (access, items, boxes). No follow-up attempt (e.g., 'what about the move itself — any concerns about how things get handled?'). No concern raised = N/A, full credit per rubric.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "we have you at about two and a half to three hours. And then yeah, so of course, if the move obviously doesn't take three hours and we could just get you at about that minimum and so as far as cost flies, yeah, it'll, it'll be an estimate around $485." — gives range (2.5–3 hrs) but does not personalize to the specific details (one-story pickup, townhome with narrow stairs and landing, 7 items + boxes).
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_beats_it_pay_less: "if the move obviously doesn't take three hours and we could just get you at about that minimum" — touched on but not fully framed as '15-min increments past the minimum' or 'you pay less.'
evidence_quotes.close: "if you have any questions or do you think it's something after the fact, you can just reply to one of our emails or just give us a shout?" — offers contact but does NOT lock rate and does NOT ask for the booking (no 'would you like our help with your move?').

top_strength: Excellent discovery logistics flow — methodically walked through pickup/delivery details, access, items, stairs, and bed assembly with genuine curiosity and note-taking; customer felt heard and comfortable.
coaching_note: Stage 2 and Stage 3 were compressed into one rapid-fire pricing moment: never called out On-Time Guarantee or Communication as differentiators, never framed the estimate with a 'ramp-up' takeaway, and closed without a rate-lock or explicit booking ask — these three moves cost ~30 pts and need to be the standard close sequence on every call.
